metric.why: At AI rack densities, the coolant loop is the machine's life support. Flow loss or a supply-temperature excursion damages hardware in seconds to minutes, far faster than an air-cooled room degrades.
metric.metric: Liquid coolant temperature and flow rate
metric.target: Facility water loops commonly deliver warmer supply temperatures than comfort cooling, which is part of why liquid cooling improves PUE.
metric.definition: Supply and return temperature and flow rate of the coolant loop, whether direct-to-chip cold plates or immersion baths.

reading.body:
Liquid coolant temperature and flow rate are the most time-critical metrics in an AI data center: a failure in either can damage hardware within seconds to minutes, far faster than air-cooled systems degrade.

At the rack densities AI workloads require, the coolant loop functions as continuous life support rather than background infrastructure. Supply-temperature excursions and flow interruptions are not slow-moving problems that operators can catch on a dashboard review cycle. They require monitoring tight enough to intervene before the damage is done.

Facility water loops for liquid cooling commonly operate at warmer supply temperatures than comfort cooling systems do, and that design choice is part of why liquid-cooled facilities achieve better power usage effectiveness. The data covers the loop itself, whether direct-to-chip cold plates or immersion baths, but does not extend to the upstream chiller plant, the outdoor heat rejection equipment, or how coolant metrics interact with the aisle-level temperature and airflow metrics tracked separately by sibling entries on this site.
